issues.description: Field 'numberOfLecturers': problem statement UML declares the attribute as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field as type byte. This discrepancy (int in problem vs byte in solution) can confuse students about the expected attribute type and may lead to inconsistent implementations or unnecessary narrowing conversions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent with the UML/problem statement: change the solution's field declaration to 'private int numberOfLecturers;'. Update any uses in the solution (constructor, getters/setters) accordingly so all artifacts use int.

issues.description: Constructor parameter for 'numberOfLecturers': the UML/problem statement specifies the attribute as int and instructs the constructor to initialize attributes in the UML order, but the solution constructor declares the 'numberOfLecturers' parameter as byte. This creates a mismatch between the expected constructor signature (int) and the solution signature (byte), potentially confusing students when they implement the constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature with the UML: change the constructor parameter type from byte to int for numberOfLecturers (e.g. public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)). Update the field type and any assignments to match.

issues.description: Setter method setNumberOfLecturers: the UML/problem statement indicates 'numberOfLecturers' is an int, but the solution provides setNumberOfLecturers(byte) accepting a byte parameter. This mismatched parameter type between UML and solution setter can mislead students about the expected setter signature and cause type inconsistencies.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the setter signature to accept an int: 'public void setNumberOfLecturers(int numberOfLecturers)'. Ensure the backing field is int and update any references. This keeps setter parameter types consistent with the UML and other getters/setters.
